facts.text: The verbal root 'Vid' in Sanskrit means 'to know'; from it the term 'Veda' was derived, which signifies 'knowledge'.
facts.quote: The verbal root 'Vid' in Sanskrit means 'to know'. From this root, the term 'Veda' was derived. It signifies 'knowledge'.

facts.text: The Vedic Hymns (Suktas or songs praising Gods) were composed by many sages (Rishis); some were composed by women.
facts.quote: The Vedic Hymns (Suktas or songs praising Gods) were composed by many sages (Rishis). Some of the Vedic Hymns were composed by women.

facts.text: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda, composed in Sanskrit.
facts.quote: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda. The Vedas are composed in Sanskrit.

facts.text: The Rigveda is the oldest of all four Vedas.
facts.quote: The Rigveda is the oldest of all four Vedas.

facts.text: The text of a Veda is called the 'Samhita'.
facts.quote: The text of Veda is called as 'Samhita'.

facts.text: The supplementary texts of every Veda are the Brahmana texts, Aranyakas and Upanishads.
facts.quote: These supplementary texts are the Brahmana texts, Aranyakas and Upanishads.

facts.text: The Brahmana texts mainly talk about sacrifices (Yajnas), worship and religious rituals and the proper manner of conducting sacrifices.
facts.quote: These texts mainly talk about the sacrifices (Yajnas), worship and religious rituals. They provide detailed descriptions regarding the proper manner of conducting sacrifices, the mantras to be recited and the meaning behind Vedic rites.

facts.text: 'Aranyaka' comes from 'Aranya', meaning 'forest'; these texts were composed for seekers of knowledge staying in the forests.
facts.quote: The term 'Aranyaka' is derived from the word 'Aranya,' meaning 'forest,' These texts were composed for seekers of knowledge staying in the forests.

facts.text: 'Upanishad' means getting knowledge by sitting close to a Guru; the Upanishads discuss Atman, Paramatman, Brahman and Vishwa.
facts.quote: The word 'Upanishad' means getting knowledge by sitting close to a Guru. These texts expound upon the philosophy about the individual soul (Atman), the Supreme Soul (Paramatman), the Ultimate Reality (Brahman) and the Universe (Vishwa).

facts.text: The Rigveda contains prayer songs dedicated to deities such as Agni, Indra and Varuna; it is the earliest Veda.
facts.quote: Characteristics: Prayer songs dedicated to deities such as Agni, Indra and Varuna. ... Significance: The earliest Veda

facts.text: The Yajurveda's main subjects are sacrifice (Yajna), fire rituals (Havans) and other rituals; it teaches about rites, rituals and religious conduct.
facts.quote: Main Subjects: Sacrifice (Yajna), fire rituals (Havans) and other rituals ... Significance: Teaches about rites, rituals and religious conduct.

facts.text: The Samaveda's main subject is the recitation of Mantras; it facilitates understanding of musical notes.
facts.quote: Main Subjects: Recitation of Mantras ... Significance: Facilitates understanding of musical notes; and recitation of Mantras

facts.text: The Atharvaveda's main subjects are way of life, agriculture and medicinal remedies; it is about health, medicines and home remedies.
facts.quote: Main Subjects: Way of life, agriculture, medicinal remedies. ... Significance: Health, medicines and home remedies, and practical wisdom.

facts.text: The Vedic period is divided into the Early Vedic Period (also called the Rigvedic Period) and the Post Vedic Period.
facts.quote: The Vedic period is broadly divided into two phases: the Early Vedic Period (also referred to as the Rigvedic Period) and the Post Vedic Period.

facts.text: The Early Vedic Period is dated to approximately 1500 BCE to 1000 BCE; the Rigveda is the primary source about it.
facts.quote: The Early Vedic Period is generally dated to approximately 1500 BCE to 1000 BCE. Our primary source of information regarding this period is Rigveda.

facts.text: In the Early Vedic Period social life was mainly based on pastoralism and the cow came to be regarded as the primary form of wealth.
facts.quote: Social life during this period was mainly based on pastoralism. Agriculture had gradually begun to emerge. During this time, the cow came to be regarded as the primary form of wealth.

facts.text: The Post Vedic Period is dated to 1000 BCE to 600 BCE, when the Vedic people migrated into the Ganges Valley.
facts.quote: The post Vedic Period is dated to 1000 BCE to 600 BCE. During this phase, the Vedic people had migrated into the Ganges Valley and established settlements there.

facts.text: In the Post Vedic Period agriculture, trade and handicrafts developed and urban centres began to emerge.
facts.quote: In this period agriculture, trade and handicrafts developed significantly. As a result of this, urban centers began to emerge.

facts.text: The family was the smallest unit of society; the head of the family was called the 'Grihapati'.
facts.quote: the family was the smallest unit of society ... The head of the family was called the 'Grihapati'.

facts.text: Several families formed a 'Gramavasahat' (village settlement); several villages formed a 'Jana' (Kingdom).
facts.quote: A group of several families formed a 'Gramavasahat' (village settlement), the group of several villages constituted a 'Jana' (Kingdom).

facts.text: The head of a village was the 'Gramani' and the head of a kingdom was the 'Rajan'.
facts.quote: The head of a village was referred to as the 'Gramani' and the head of a kingdom was called the 'Rajan'.

facts.text: Everyone was expected to follow righteousness (Dharma), truth and justice.
facts.quote: It was considered essential for everyone in the society to adhere to the following principles: righteousness (Dharma), truth and justice.

facts.text: Vedic society was structured into four Varnas: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra.
facts.quote: Vedic society was structured into four Varnas : Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra.

facts.text: Students stayed in the Guru's Ashram (Gurukul) and studied the Vedas, Mathematics, Astronomy, Ayurveda, Ethics and weaponry.
facts.quote: Students stayed in the Guru's Ashram and studied. In the Gurukul, students had to live a disciplined life. ... Students studied subjects like the Vedas, Mathematics, Astronomy, Ayurveda, Ethics and the weaponry.

facts.text: Education also aimed to inculcate humility, discipline, righteousness and self-control.
facts.quote: The objective of education was not just to acquire knowledge but also to inculcate values like humility, discipline, righteousness and self-control.

facts.text: Under the Ashram system, a person's life was divided into four distinct stages.
facts.quote: Under this system, a person's life was divided into four distinct stages.

facts.text: The Brahmacharyashram was the first stage of life, when a child received education under the guidance of a Guru.
facts.quote: The Brahmacharyashram is considered the first stage of life. During this stage, a child was supposed to receive education under guidance of Guru.

facts.text: After education a person entered the Grihasthashram, to marry and fulfil domestic duties and social responsibilities.
facts.quote: After completing their education, a person would enter the Grihasthashram. It was important in this stage to marry and fulfill domestic duties and social responsibilities.

facts.text: In the Vanaprasthashram one withdrew from the family for meditation, penance and philosophical thinking.
facts.quote: After fulfilling responsibilities of a householder, at this stage of Vanaprasthashram one was expected to withdraw from the family and engage in meditation, penance and philosophical thinking.

facts.text: The Sanyasashram was the concluding stage; a person renounced all relations and did not stay at one place for long.
facts.quote: The Sanyasashram was considered the concluding stage of life. At this stage, a person was expected to renounce all relations ... A person was not supposed to stay at one place for long time.

facts.text: Vedic people valued truthfulness, self-control and generosity; harmony with nature and honouring manual labour marked Vedic society.
facts.quote: They were taught the importance of values such as truthfulness, self-control and generosity. ... Harmony with nature and honouring manual labor was characteristic of Vedic society.

facts.text: The Vedic diet had grains, milk, curd, ghee, honey and vegetables, with barley, wheat, rice and millet; it was plant-based.
facts.quote: Their diet consisted of grains, milk, curd, ghee, honey and vegetables. They used various foodgrains such as barley, wheat, rice and millet in their meals. Thus, their diet consisted of plant-based foods.

facts.text: Ancient Indian medical science promotes a balanced diet, yoga and physical and mental well-being, which boosts immunity.
facts.quote: Ancient Indian medical science promotes a balanced diet, yoga and both physical and mental well-being. This helps to boost immunity.

facts.text: Vedic people played archery, chariot racing, wrestling and board games like Saripata (a game like chess).
facts.quote: They played games such as archery, chariot racing, wrestling and board games like Saripata (a game like chess).

facts.text: Musical notes (swaras) were essential during the recitation of Vedic texts; the Samaveda dwells on this aspect.
facts.quote: Musical notes (swaras) were considered essential during the recitation of Vedic texts. ... Samaveda dwells on this particular aspect.

facts.text: Musical instruments such as Veena, Mridanga, Shankha (conch shell) and Bansuri were widely used.
facts.quote: musical instruments such as Veena, Mridanga, Shankha (conch shell) and Bansuri were widely used.

facts.text: Vedic music formed the base of Indian classical music.
facts.quote: Vedic music formed the base of Indian classical music, which evolved later.

facts.text: Women were honoured in Early Vedic society and could study the Vedas; Lopamudra, Ghosha, Gargi, Maitreyi and Apala were famous female scholars.
facts.quote: Women were honoured in the Early Vedic society. ... Just like men, women had the freedom to study the Vedas. Lopamudra, Ghosha, Gargi, Maitreyi and Apala are some examples of famous female scholars from that period.

facts.text: In the post-Vedic period society became increasingly patriarchal and the freedom of women was reduced gradually.
facts.quote: However, during the post-Vedic period, society became increasingly patriarchal. Restrictions were imposed on women's education. The freedom of women was reduced gradually.

facts.text: Economic life was based on agriculture and animal husbandry; the cow was used as a means of exchange.
facts.quote: The economic life of the people during Vedic period was based on agriculture and animal husbandry. ... The cow was used as means of exchange.

facts.text: Horses were important for warfare and sacrificial rituals; oxen were used for ploughing and transportation.
facts.quote: Horses were important for warfare and sacrificial rituals, while oxen were employed for ploughing and transportation.

facts.text: Occupations included metalworking, pottery, weaving, goldsmythy and chariot-building; trade was done through barter.
facts.quote: Animal husbandry, metalworking, pottery, weaving, goldsmythy and chariot-building were some of the significant occupations. Trade was gradually developing and transactions were made through barter.

facts.text: Groups of merchants and artisans were called 'Shreni' and their head was the 'Shreshthi'.
facts.quote: The groups of merchants and artisans were known as 'Shreni' and their head was known as the 'Shreshthi'.

facts.text: Religion was based on nature worship: Fire (Agni), water (Varuna), Wind (Marut), Sun (Surya), Dawn (Usha), Earth (Prithvi) and Moon (Soma).
facts.quote: For example, Fire (Agni), water (Varuna), Wind (Marut), Sun (Surya), Dawn (Usha), Earth (Prithvi) and Moon (Soma).

facts.text: Indra was considered the most powerful of all deities.
facts.quote: Indra was considered the most powerful of all deities.

facts.text: The 'Havi' (Ahuti) offered in a Yajna was believed to reach the deities through fire; food, ghee and grains were offered.
facts.quote: It was believed that the 'Havi' (Ahuti) offered in a Yajna reached the deities through the medium of fire. Food, ghee and grains were offered as Havi during Yajna.

facts.text: The foundation of the Vedic way of life was truth, justice and 'Rut', the principle of maintaining the sanctity of the natural cycle of life.
facts.quote: The foundation of Vedic way of life was truth, justice and 'Rut' the principle of maintaining the sanctity of the natural cycle of life.

facts.text: The Indian Navy motto 'Sham No Varunah' is from a verse in the Upanishads and means 'May the deity Varuna protect us.'
facts.quote: The motto inscribed on the emblem of the Indian Navy - 'Sham No Varunah' ... is taken from a verse in the Upanishads. This phrase can be translated as: "May the deity Varuna protect us."

facts.text: After independence, Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari proposed this motto; the new Navy emblem is inspired by the Royal Seal of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: the then Governor-General, C. Rajagopalachari, proposed this specific motto. The new emblem of the Indian Navy is inspired by the Royal Seal of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: The Sabha (council of elders and senior individuals) and the Samiti (group of common people) advised the King.
facts.quote: These two bodies were known as the 'Sabha' and the 'Samiti.' The 'Sabha' was a council comprising elders and distinguished senior individuals ... The 'Samiti' was the group of common people of the village or community.

facts.text: The 'Vidatha' and 'Jana' also guided the King; women took an active part in the Sabha and the Vidatha.
facts.quote: The institutions known as the 'Vidatha' and 'Jana' also served to guide and counsel the King. Women also played an active role in the proceedings and functioning of the Sabha and the 'Vidatha'.

facts.text: Important officials were the Priest (Purohit), Commander-in-Chief (Senapti) and Head of the Assembly (Sabhapati).
facts.quote: The Priest (Purohit), Commander-in-Chief (Senapti) and Head of the Assembly (Sabhapati) were officials of particular importance.

facts.text: The 'Bhagdugh' collected the King's 'share' (bhaga).
facts.quote: The official known as 'Bhagdugh' was appointed to collect the King's 'share' (bhaga).

facts.text: In war the King led the army; he did not have absolute power and governed by the counsel of the Sabha and the Samiti.
facts.quote: During times of war, the King himself led the army. ... Though the King was the head of the state, he did not possess absolute power. He used to govern in accordance with the counsel of the Sabha and the Samiti.

facts.text: Shankaracharya Shri Bharati Krishna Tirtha wrote 'Vedic Mathematics'; its formula 'Nikhilam navatascharamam Dashatah' gives 98 x 99 = 9702.
facts.quote: Shankaracharya Shri Bharati Krishna Tirtha has written a book entitled, 'Vedic Mathematics'. ... A formula given in the book 'Vedic Mathematics' is 'Nikhilam navatascharamam Dashatah'. ... Thus, Answer is 98 x 99 = 9702
